TABATABAI:6:74-83#14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#14/r2.claim: Because God creates all things, His ownership cannot be shared, transferred, or delegated so as to make Him unnecessary.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#14/r2.anchor: وهو بمعنى ملكه الذي لا يشاركه فيه غيره ولا يزول عنه إلى غيره ولا يقبل نقلا ولا تفويضا

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r5.claim: The passage exposes the baselessness of Quraysh's idols and intercessors, which they viewed as sources of success and feared abandoning.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p516/r5.anchor: that if they left them, they would be destroyed.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p320/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p320/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p320/r4.claim: The people of Paradise praise God with several formulas; their praise is delight rather than an obligation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p320/r4.anchor: والتحميد هنالك على سبيل اللذة، لا التكليف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p320/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p320/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p320/r5.claim: A hadith says the people of Paradise will be inspired to glorify and sanctify God; no transmitter or grading is supplied here.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p320/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p320/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p320/r7.claim: “His is the judgment” means His decree and His deciding between His servants; araytum means “tell me.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p320/r7.anchor: وله الحكم: أي القضاء بين عباده والفصل.

ASAD-NOTES:28:68#n75/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:68#n75/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:68#n75/r1.claim: Asad offers an alternate rendering: God's praise is due in this present life as well as in the life to come.
ASAD-NOTES:28:68#n75/r1.anchor: in this first [i.e., present life] as well as in the life to come

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:68/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:68/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:68/r4.claim: The author renders the phrase as praise belonging to God both before and after.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:68/r4.anchor: “Önünde de sonunda da hamd O’na mahsustur” diye çevirdiğimiz 70. âyetteki cümleyi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:68/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:68/r5.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:68/r5.claim: Commentators interpret the phrase to mean that praise belongs to God in this world and the hereafter.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:68/r5.anchor: müfessirler, “Bu dünyada da âhirette de hamd O’na mahsustur” şeklinde yorumlamışlardır

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p565/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p565/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p565/r2.claim: The verse sums up the discussion: God alone is truly God and all other supposed deities are baseless, refuting Arabs who accepted God as supreme while still assigning Him partners.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p565/r2.anchor: This verse sums up the previous discussion: He alone is the rea l God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p565/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p565/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p565/r3.claim: All favors in this life and the Hereafter come from God, so He alone deserves gratitude and no one else shares in it; the praise of Paradise's people is also referenced in Sūrah Yūnus.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p565/r3.anchor: gratitude and in the Hereafter too. No one else will have any  share in it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p565/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p565/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p565/r4.claim: Only the Almighty decides every person's affairs, and everyone returns to Him alone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p565/r4.anchor: only the Almighty will have the authority of deciding the affairs of each and every person and everyone will come to Him and none else.

BURSEVI:v6p309/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p309/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p309/r1.claim: The Ottoman sultans are the final dynasty and will continue into the time of the awaited Mahdi, according to what major scholars have established as sound.
BURSEVI:v6p309/r1.anchor: ومن الملوك الخواقين العثمانية لأن دولتهم آخر الدول وتتصل بزمان المهدي المنتظر

BURSEVI:v6p309/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p309/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p309/r2.claim: The author favors scholars who unite outward and inward knowledge, and prays for steadfastness on the path of realization.
BURSEVI:v6p309/r2.anchor: واختار من العلماء من تشرف بعلم الظاهر والباطن وكان ذا جناحين نسأل الله الثبات في طريق التحقيق

BURSEVI:v6p309/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p309/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p309/r5.claim: Only God deserves worship; He alone possesses divinity and lordship, with no equal or comparable being.
BURSEVI:v6p309/r5.anchor: لا أحد يستحقها إلا هو وهو المتوحد بعز إلهيته المتفرد بجلال ربوبيته

BURSEVI:v6p309/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p309/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p309/r6.claim: God deserves praise for His greatness and thanks for His favors in this world and the next, since He grants every present and future blessing to all creation.
BURSEVI:v6p309/r6.anchor: استحقاقا على عظمته والشكر استيجابا على نعمته {فى الاولى} أي الدنيا {والاخرة}

BURSEVI:v6p309/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p309/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p309/r7.claim: Believers will praise God in the afterlife with joy and delight, without burden.
BURSEVI:v6p309/r7.anchor: يحمده المؤمنون في الآخرة كما حمدوه في الدنيا بقولهم

BURSEVI:v6p309/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p309/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p309/r8.claim: God alone has the effective decree over what He creates, chooses, honors, humiliates, gives life to, and causes to die.
BURSEVI:v6p309/r8.anchor: فيما يخلق ويختار ويعز ويذل ويحيي ويميت أي القضاء النافذ في كل شيء

BURSEVI:v6p309/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p309/r9.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v6p309/r9.claim: Kashf al-Asrar says God's effective judgment governs both worlds and all creatures ultimately return to His judgment in the next.
BURSEVI:v6p309/r9.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : وله الحكم النافذ في الدنيا والآخرة ومصير الخلق كلهم

BURSEVI:v6p309/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p309/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v6p309/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says God decrees forgiveness for the obedient and misery and woe for the disobedient.
BURSEVI:v6p309/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : حكم لأهل طاعته بالمغفرة ولأهل معصيته بالشقاء والويل

BURSEVI:v6p309/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p309/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p309/r11.claim: All people return to God through resurrection, and to no other.

BURSEVI:v6p309/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p309/r12.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p309/r12.claim: The Najmiyya reading distinguishes a voluntary return through spiritual journey, following, and arrival in the Divine Presence, reserved for humans, from an involuntary return through death, resurrection, judgment, and recompense.
BURSEVI:v6p309/r12.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {وإليه ترجعون} بالاختيار أو بالاضطرار فأما بالاختيار فهو الرجوع إلى الحضرة

QIRAAT-ER:28:70:19#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:28:70:19#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:28:70:19#1/r1.claim: The active reading makes the return self-initiated by humans instead of passively imposed by God.
QIRAAT-ER:28:70:19#1/r1.anchor: the return becomes a self-initiated act rather than an imposed one

QASHANI:28:67-70/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:67-70/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:67-70/r5.claim: There is no god but God and no partner with Him in existence.

QASHANI:28:67-70/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:67-70/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:67-70/r6.claim: All absolute praise belongs to God: every manifest and hidden perfection in the forms of the cosmos belongs to Him, so worldly beauty, wealth, strength, and honor are His manifestations.
QASHANI:28:67-70/r6.anchor: المطلق لثبوت جميع الكمالات الظاهرة على مظاهر الأكوان

QASHANI:28:67-70/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:67-70/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:67-70/r7.claim: Likewise, every complete knower and gnostic in the afterlife manifests His perfection, knowledge, and recognition.
QASHANI:28:67-70/r7.anchor: وكل كامل عالم عارف به في الآخرة بكماله وعلمه ومعرفته

QASHANI:28:67-70/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:67-70/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:67-70/r8.claim: God's judgment compels all things to His will: worldly ugliness, poverty, weakness, and lowliness fall under His rule and subjugation.
QASHANI:28:67-70/r8.anchor: يقهر كل شيء على مقتضى مشيئته ويحكم عليه بموجب إرادته

QASHANI:28:67-70/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:67-70/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:67-70/r9.claim: In the afterlife, all who remain veiled are forsaken, captive, and rejected under His judgment.
QASHANI:28:67-70/r9.anchor: وكل محجوب مخذول، أسير، مردود في الآخرة في قهره وتحت حكمه

QASHANI:28:67-70/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:67-70/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:67-70/r10.claim: Returning to God means annihilation in His existence, acts, attributes, or Essence.
QASHANI:28:67-70/r10.anchor: بالفناء في وجوده أو أفعاله وصفاته أو ذاته

QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r6.claim: God alone is one in the majesty of His lordship, with no likeness or equal.
QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r6.anchor: توحد بعز هيبته ، وتفرد بجلال ربوبيته ، لا شبيه يساويه ، ولا نظير يضاهيه

QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r7.claim: God deserves praise for His gifts and thanks for His favor: He is praised in this life and thanked in the next.
QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r7.anchor: { له الحمد } استحقاقا على عطيته ، وله الشكر استيجابا على نعمته ؛ ففي الدنيا المحمود الله ، وفي العقبى المشكور الله

QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r8.claim: Every good comes from God: beneficence follows His sovereignty, blessing His mercy, and victory His power.
QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r8.anchor: فالإحسان من الله لأن السلطان لله ، والنعمة من الله لأن الرحمة لله ، والنصرة من الله لأن القدرة لله

QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r9.claim: Only God brings the dawn after spiritual nights: repentance after lapse, existence after seeking, expansion after constriction, and union after separation; He also gives the night in which servants rest in seclusion with Him.
QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r9.anchor: إن دامت ليالي الفترة فمن الذي يأتي بنهار التوبة غير الله

QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r10.claim: When communion's daylight persists, detractors cannot spoil its joy; this too is among the states whose continuance depends on God.
QUSHAYRI:v2p443/r10.anchor: إن دام في الوصلة نهاركم فأي سبيل للواشين إلى تنغيص سروركم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r1.claim: God alone possesses divinity; the declaration that there is no deity but Him confirms that exclusive status, as “the Kaaba is the qibla” can be restated “there is no qibla but it.”
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r1.anchor: وهو تعالى المستأثر بالألوهية المختص بها وقوله سبحانه : ( لا إله إلا هو ( تقرير لذلك كقولك : الكعبة القبلة لا قبلة إلا هي

ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r2.claim: Praise in both worlds belongs to God alone because He originates every blessing, while other agents are only means; here praise refers especially to response for blessings, as the next verse indicates.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r2.anchor: له تعالى ذلك دون غيره سبحانه لأنه جل جلاله المعطي لجميع النعم بالذات وما سواه وسائط

ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r3.claim: Some say praise is broader than gratitude and that exclusivity applies to the two worlds together: others share in worldly praise, but only God receives praise in the hereafter.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r3.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن الحمد هنا أعم من الشكر واعتبر الحصر بالنسبة إلى مجموع حمدي الدارين

ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r4.claim: Al-Alusi rejects that restriction: even virtues and beautiful qualities are God's creation, so praise for them ultimately belongs to Him; even in the hereafter, the Prophet is praised at the great intercession.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r4.anchor: وفيه أن الحمد مطلقا مختص به تعالى لأن الفضائل والأوصاف الجميلة كلها بخلقه تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r5.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r5.claim: Several exegetes explain hereafter praise through believers' statements praising God for fulfilling His promise, removing grief, and being Lord of all worlds; they say this praise is delight, not a burden.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r5.anchor: وفسر غير واحد حمده تعالى في الآخرة بقول المؤمنين : ( الحمد لله الذي صدقنا وعده ) وقولهم : ( الحمد لله الذي أذهب عنا الحزن )

ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r6.speaker: جابر
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r6.claim: A hadith in Muslim and Abu Dawud, from Jabir describing the people of Paradise, says they are inspired to glorify and proclaim God's oneness as naturally as breathing.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r6.anchor: وفي حديث رواه مسلم وأبو داود عن جابر في وصف أهل الجنة يلهمون التسبيح والتهليل كما يلهمون النفس

ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r7.claim: God alone has the effective judgment and decree over everything, with no partner sharing it.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r7.anchor: القضاء النافذ في كل شيء من غير مشاركة فيه لغيره تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains that God judges among His servants, granting forgiveness and favor to the obedient and misery and woe to the disobedient.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r8.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أي له الحكم بين عباده تعالى فيحكم لأهل طاعته بالمغفرة والفضل ولأهل معصيته بالشقاء والويل

ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r9.claim: The verse closes by saying all return to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p106#2/r9.anchor: وإليه ( سبحانه لا إلى غيره + ( ( ترجعون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p218#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p218#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p218#2/r2.claim: God alone is deity; His allies praise Him in this world and praise Him in Paradise in the Hereafter.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p218#2/r2.anchor: يحمده أولياؤه في الدنيا، ويحمدونه في الآخرة في الجنة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p218#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p218#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p218#2/r3.claim: God’s judgment is His deciding among all creatures.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p218#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p218#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p218#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says God judges those who obey Him with forgiveness and those who disobey with misery.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p218#2/r4.anchor: حكم لأهل طاعته بالمغفرة ولأهل معصيته بالشقاء،

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:70-72/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:70-72/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:70-72/r1.claim: God alone deserves worship; none but Him is worthy of it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:70-72/r1.anchor: المستحق للعبادة. { لا إله إلا هو } لا أحد يستحقها إلا هو

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:70-72/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:70-72/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:70-72/r2.claim: All praise belongs to Him because He grants every immediate and ultimate favor; believers praise Him in the next life as in this life, rejoicing in His favor and delighting in praise.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:70-72/r2.anchor: لأنه المولى للنعم كلها عاجلها وآجلها يحمده المؤمنون في الآخرة كما حمدوه في الدنيا

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:70-72/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:70-72/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:70-72/r3.claim: God's judgment is an effective decree over everything, and return to Him occurs through resurrection.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:70-72/r3.anchor: القضاء النافذ في كل شيء. { وإليه ترجعون } بالنشور

BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r1.claim: God's will governs what happens; the people have no independent choice to obtain whatever they select, such as a messenger bearing Moses' signs.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r1.anchor: أي أن يفعلوا أو يفعل لهم كل ما يختارونه من إتيان الرسول بمثل ما أتىى به موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام أو غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r2.claim: Al-khiyara can mean the act of choosing or the chosen object; using the result for its cause captures the idea that without God's choice it is fruitless and void.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r2.anchor: اسم من الاختيار , يقام مقام المصدرن وهو أيضا اسم المختار

BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r3.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r3.claim: Al-Razi cites this as evidence that a servant is not independently free in his choice.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r3.anchor: قال الرازي في اللوامع : وفيه دليل على أن العبد في اختياره غير مختار

BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r4.claim: The contented entrust matters to God: they hasten to commands, endure affliction, and accept both honor and abasement, wanting only what He wills.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r4.anchor: فإن أمرهم أو نهاهم بادروا , وإن أصابهم بسهام المصائب العظام صابروا , وإن أعزهم أعزوا أنفسهم وأكرموا , وإن أذلهم رضول وسلموا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r5.claim: The cited verses illustrate that the contented person wants only what God wills and accepts blame out of love for Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r5.anchor: وقف الهوى بي حيث أنت فليس لي متأخر عنه لا متقدم أجد الملامة في هواك لذيذة حبا لذكرك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r6.claim: It would be a defect for something to occur against God's will; associating partners implies weakness, so God is exalted above others having a will that can be carried out independently.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r6.anchor: ولما كان إيقاع شيء على غير مراده نقصا , وكان وقوع الشرك سفولا وعجزا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r7.claim: God knows hidden thoughts, including whether people would believe if given signs like Moses' and whether professed belief is sincere, as well as what they disclose.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r7.anchor: من كونهم يؤمنون على تقدير أن تأتيهم آيات مثل ىيات موسى أو لا يؤمنون

BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r8.claim: God alone is the deity and possesses praise in both worlds, whether people believe or disbelieve.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r8.anchor: عبر عن ذلك بقوله : { وهو الله } أي المستأثر بالإلهية الذي لا سمي له

BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r9.claim: God alone executes judgment absolutely; if He willed, He could compel people to believe.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r9.anchor: أي إمضاء القضاء على الإطلاق , فلو أراد لقسرهم على الإيمان

BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r10.claim: Everyone returns to God at the trumpet blast and resurrection, and all present decisions are also subject to His enactment or reversal.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r10.anchor: أي بأيسر أمر يوم النفخ في الصور , لبعثرة القبور , بالعث والنشورن

BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r11.claim: These verses fortify the obedient by affirming God's knowledge of everything, His freedom from defects, and His just recompense of obedient and disobedient people.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p512/r11.anchor: ففي الآيات غاية التقوية لقلوب المطيعين , علما بكل المعلومات , منزها عن النقائص والآفات يجزي الطائعين والعاصين بالقسط

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3002#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3002#2/r1.speaker: كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3002#2/r1.claim: Kaʿb glosses praise of God as praise directed to God.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3002#2/r1.anchor: عن كعب قال : الحمد لله ، ثناء لله

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3002#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3002#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3002#2/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak calls praise the cloak of the All-Merciful.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3002#2/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك ، قال : الحمد رداء الرحمن

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3002#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3002#2/r3.speaker: عزيز
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3002#2/r3.claim: In a report from ʿAziz, God judges without injustice, restores rights between the weak and powerful, and shows the gathered people their contrasting eternal outcomes.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3002#2/r3.anchor: قال عزيز : يتجلى الله تبارك وتعالى العلي على كرسي الكبرياء والنور ، ويحكم بين العباد حكما ليس فيه ظلم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3002#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3002#2/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3002#2/r4.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya explains that people return to God after life.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3002#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي العالية واليه ترجعون قال : ترجعون اليه بعد الحياة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p166/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p166/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p166/r7.claim: Verse 70 continues the account of creation and choice; its main point is that judgment belongs to God, with the preceding description proving His exclusive rule and embedding His majesty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p166/r7.anchor: وإنما قدم عليه ما هو دليل على أنه المنفرد بالحكم مع إدماج صفات عظمته الذاتية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p167/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p167/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p167/r1.claim: The opening pronoun refers back to the One described from 28:58 onward, and the divine name is its predicate; this prevents confusion or assigning the name’s qualities elsewhere.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p167/r1.anchor: أي الموصوف بتلك الصفات العظيمة والفاعل لتلك الأفعال الجليلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p167/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p167/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p167/r2.claim: “There is no god but Him” further establishes that the named God alone is truly divine; polytheists wrongly assign divinity to idols, so the statement refutes shirk after its eschatological exposure in 28:64.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p167/r2.anchor: وفي هذا الخبر الثاني زيادة تقرير لمدلول الخبر الأول فإن اسم الجلالة اختص بالدلالة على الإله الحق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p167/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p167/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p167/r3.claim: Exclusive praise in both abodes proves no other is divine: even polytheists praise only God; the lām denotes possession, fronting gives true exclusivity, and generic al-ḥamd encompasses all praise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p167/r3.anchor: وهو استدلال على انتفاء إلهية غيره بحجة أن الناس مؤمنهم وكافرهم لا يحمدون في الدنيا إلا الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p167/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p167/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p167/r4.claim: Al-ūlā means this world, where praise of others is figurative; the verse’s afterlife praise is genuine and is illustrated by 17:52.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p167/r4.anchor: هي الدنيا وتخصيص الحمد به في الدنيا اختصاص لجنس الحمد به لأن حمد غيره مجاز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p168/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p168/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p168/r1.claim: “To Him belongs judgment” uses possession and fronting for exclusivity; judgment is assigning benefit or harm, with its object understood as both abodes. Other worldly judgment is figurative, while judgment in the afterlife belongs only to God, refuting idols and their alleged intercession.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p168/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p168/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p168/r2.claim: “To Him you return” specifies afterlife return after the general mention of all praise and judgment: people will glorify Him and undergo His rule, obliging them to affirm resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p168/r2.anchor: أي أنكم ترجعون إليه في الآخرة فتمجدونه ويجري عليكم حكمه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p168/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p168/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p168/r3.claim: The fronted “to Him” serves the rhyme and emphasizes the final arrival at His judgment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p168/r3.anchor: للرعاية على الفاصلة وللاهتمام بالانتهاء إليه أي إلى حكمه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p296#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p296#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p296#2/r3.claim: God alone is divine; He merits praise in both lives because of His attributes, and “judgment” means deciding and resolving affairs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p296#2/r3.anchor: ثم أفرد نفسه بالألوهية ونفاها عن سواه، وأخبر أن الحمد له في الدنيا والآخرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p296#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p296#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p296#2/r4.claim: The verse then declares that all creatures will return to God and be resurrected.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.claim: Hasan, Ata, and Ikrima hold that all of al-Qasas is Meccan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة أنها مكية كلها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p238/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p238/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p238/r1.claim: God's allies praise Him in this world and will praise Him in Paradise.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p238/r1.anchor: أي يحمده أولياؤه في الدنيا ويحمدونه في الجنة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p238/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p238/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p238/r2.claim: God's judgment means His decision among all creatures.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p238/r2.anchor: وله الحكم وهو الفصل بين الخلائق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p251#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p251#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p251#2/r1.claim: God alone has divinity and is the only one worshipped, just as He alone creates and chooses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p251#2/r1.anchor: أي: هو المنفرد بالإلهية، فلا معبود سواه، كما لا رب يخلق ويختار سواه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p251#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p251#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p251#2/r2.claim: God deserves praise in this life and the next for everything He does, because His acts are just and wise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p251#2/r2.anchor: في جميع ما يفعله هو المحمود عليه، لعدله وحكمته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p251#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p251#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p251#2/r3.claim: God's judgment cannot be overturned, owing to His might, dominance, wisdom, and mercy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p251#2/r3.anchor: الذي لا معقب له، لقهره وغلبته وحكمته ورحمته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p251#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p251#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p251#2/r4.claim: All people return to God on Judgment Day, where He repays each person for good or evil and nothing of their deeds is hidden from Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p251#2/r4.anchor: جميعكم يوم القيامة فيجازي (2) كل عامل بعمله، من خير وشر، ولا يخفى عليه منهم خافية في سائر الأعمال.

JISHUMI:v8p5522/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5522/r23.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5522/r23.claim: God alone is deity and deserves praise in this world and the next because the blessings of both come from Him.
JISHUMI:v8p5522/r23.anchor: له الحمد في الأولى أي: الدنيا والآخرة أي: هو يستحق الحمد في الدارين؛ لأن نعم الدارين منه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p244#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p244#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p244#6/r1.claim: God alone possesses divinity; the phrase no god but He reinforces this, like saying the qibla is the Kaaba and there is no qibla but it.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p244#6/r1.anchor: تقدير لذلك كقولك القبلة الكعبة لا قبلة إلا هي

NASAFI-FULL:v3p244#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p244#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p244#6/r2.claim: Praise belongs to God in this world and the Hereafter; the saved praise Him for relief from grief, fulfilled promise, and as Lord of the worlds.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p244#6/r2.anchor: هو قولهم الحمد لله الذي أذهب عنا الحزن الحمد لله الذي

NASAFI-FULL:v3p244#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p244#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p244#6/r3.claim: In the Hereafter, praising God is pleasure rather than an onerous duty.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p244#6/r3.anchor: والتحميد ثمة على وجه اللذة لا الكلفة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p244#6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p244#6/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p244#6/r4.claim: God judges between His servants, and they return to Him through resurrection.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p244#6/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p244#6/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p244#6/r5.claim: Yaqub reads the return verb with open tāʾ and kasra on the jīm.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:68-70/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:68-70/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:68-70/r6.claim: Subhana means declaring God transcendent, while taala means He is holy and glorified above what they associate with Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:68-70/r6.anchor: أي تنزيها. { وتعالى } أي تقدس وتمجد

QURTUBI-FULL:28:68-70/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:68-70/r7.speaker: ابن محيصن وحميد
QURTUBI-FULL:28:68-70/r7.claim: Ibn Muhaysin and Humayd read takun with fatḥa on the tāʾ and ḍamma on the kāf.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:68-70/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن وحميد: «تكن» بفتح التاء وضم الكاف.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:68-70/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:68-70/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:68-70/r8.claim: God praises Himself as knowing the hidden and the visible, uniquely divine, the sole recipient of praise and ruler, and the one to whom all return.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:68-70/r8.anchor: تمدح سبحانه بأنه عالم الغيب والشهادة لا يخفى عليه شيء { وهو الله لا إله إلا هو له الحمد في الأولى والآخرة وله الحكم وإليه ترجعون

RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r1.claim: Since reward is not owed to God’s creatures but is given by grace, God deserves praise in this life and the next; the people of Paradise praise Him in three cited verses.
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r1.anchor: الثواب غير واجب عليه بل هو سبحانه يعطيه فضلا وإحسانا فله الحمد في الأولى والآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r2.claim: The Muʿtazilites say reward is owed, so the people of Paradise do not owe praise for receiving it, while the people of Hell received no favor warranting praise.
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r2.anchor: أما المعتزلة فعندهم الثواب مستحق فلا يستحق الحمد بفعله من أهل الجنة ، وأما أهل النار فما أنعم عليهم حتى يستحق الحمد منهم

RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r3.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r3.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues that even the people of Hell owe God praise and thanks for worldly enablement, facilitation, kindness, and other blessings, which wrongdoing does not erase.
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r3.anchor: قال القاضي إنه يستحق الحمد والشكر من أهل النار أيضا بما فعله بهم في الدنيا من التمكين والتيسير والإلطاف وسائر النعم

RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r4.claim: Rāzī objects that afterlife dwellers necessarily know repentance must be accepted and gratitude earns reward; able to act and aware it saves them, they would repent and give thanks, ending their punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r4.anchor: لأن أهل الآخرة مضطرون إلى معرفة الحق فإذا علموا بالضرورة أن التوبة عن القبائح يجب على الله قبولها وعلموا بالضرورة أن الاشتغال بالشكر الواجب عليهم يوجب على الله الثواب

RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r5.claim: ‘His is the judgment’ can mean worldly authority: every creature’s rule takes effect only through God’s ruling, including masters, husbands, parents, rulers, and the Messenger.
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r5.anchor: فأما في الدنيا فحكم كل أحد سواه إنما نفذ بحكمه ، فلولا حكمه لما نفذ على العبد حكم سيده ولا على الزوجة حكم زوجها ولا على الابن حكم أبيه

RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r6.claim: Alternatively, ‘His is the judgment’ refers to the afterlife, where God judges among servants and secures justice for the oppressed against oppressors.
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r6.anchor: وأما في الآخرة فلا شك أنه هو الحاكم ، لأنه الذي يتولى الحكم بين العباد في الآخرة ، فينتصف للمظلومين من الظالمين

RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r7.claim: Returning to God means returning to the realm of His judgment and decree; the preposition marks an endpoint, while God is beyond place and direction.
RAZI-FULL:v25p10/r7.anchor: وإلى محل حكمه وقضائه ترجعون ، فإن كلمة إلى لانتهاء الغاية وهو تعالى منزه من المكان والجهة

STUDYQURAN:28:70/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:70/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:70/r1.claim: Praise at the beginning and end can refer either to the beginning and end of time or to this world and the next.
STUDYQURAN:28:70/r1.anchor: At the beginning and at the end can mean at the beginning and end of

STUDYQURAN:28:70/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:70/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:70/r2.claim: Al-ākhirah may mean the last and is usually rendered the Hereafter, especially in contrast with al-dunyā, literally the lower or nearer.
STUDYQURAN:28:70/r2.anchor: The end renders al-ākhirah, which can also mean “the last” and is usually rendered

STUDYQURAN:28:70/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:70/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:70/r3.claim: Here al-ākhirah is paired with al-ūlā, which can also mean the first.

STUDYQURAN:28:70/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:70/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:70/r4.claim: Ḥukm denotes judgment and can also carry the senses of decision-making power, dominion, rule, or wisdom.
STUDYQURAN:28:70/r4.anchor: Judgment here renders ḥukm, which can also convey the sense of the power of decision, dominion, or rule as well as wisdom.

STUDYQURAN:28:70/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:70/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:70/r5.claim: All rightful judgment and power in this world operate through God's judgment and power; in the Hereafter God judges directly among His creatures, to whom they return.
STUDYQURAN:28:70/r5.anchor: In this world, all judgment and power are rightfully exercised only as a function of God’s Judgment and Power,

TABATABAI:28:68-70/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:68-70/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:68-70/r4.claim: The preceding statement is followed by God’s knowledge of hidden and open thoughts to show that He chooses for them with knowledge of their inward and outward sins, purifying them through His wisdom.
TABATABAI:28:68-70/r4.anchor: إنما اختار لهم ما اختار لعلمه بما في ظاهرهم وباطنهم من أوساخ الشرك والمعصية

TABATABAI:28:68-70/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:68-70/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:68-70/r5.claim: The opening pronoun refers to ‘your Lord’ in the prior verse; the definite name Allah alludes to a description, and ‘no god but He’ reinforces that only He is divine.
TABATABAI:28:68-70/r5.anchor: الضمير في صدر الآية راجع إلى { ربك } في الآية السابقة

TABATABAI:28:68-70/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:68-70/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:68-70/r6.claim: The verse completes the argument that God alone may command exclusive worship: He alone is divine and knows their hidden and visible states.
TABATABAI:28:68-70/r6.anchor: وهو الإله المستحق للعبادة وحده فيجب عليهم أن يعبدوه وحده

TABATABAI:28:68-70/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:68-70/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:68-70/r7.claim: God alone merits worship because every perfection and blessing in both worlds comes from Him, and all praise for them ultimately returns to Him; worship is praise in word or deed.
TABATABAI:28:68-70/r7.anchor: والعبادة ثناء بقول أو فعل فهو المعبود المستحق للعبادة وحده

TABATABAI:28:68-70/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:68-70/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:68-70/r8.claim: God alone merits worship because He is absolute owner in creation and legislation, and may command His servants to worship Him alone.
TABATABAI:28:68-70/r8.anchor: وهو سبحانه مالك في مرحلة التشريع والاعتبار كما أنه مالك في مرحلة التكوين والحقيقة

TABATABAI:28:68-70/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:68-70/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:68-70/r9.claim: Since all return to God for accounting and recompense and He alone judges, He alone must be worshipped and His religion followed.
TABATABAI:28:68-70/r9.anchor: وإذ كان هو المحاسب المجازي وحده فهو الذي يجب أن يعبد وحده وله دين يجب أن يتعبد به وحده

TABRISI:28:67-70/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:67-70/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:67-70/r9.claim: God alone deserves worship; all praise belongs to Him in this world and the next for His blessings, and judgment distinguishing truth from falsehood is His.
TABRISI:28:67-70/r9.anchor: لا يستحق العبادة سواه { له الحمد في الأولى والآخرة } أي له الثناء المدح والتعظيم على ما أنعم به على خلقه في الدنيا والعقبى

TABRISI:28:67-70/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:67-70/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:28:67-70/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God judges the obedient with forgiveness and favor, and the disobedient with misery and woe.
TABRISI:28:67-70/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يحكم لأهل طاعته بالمغفرة والفضل ولأهل معصيته بالشقاء والويل

TABRISI:28:67-70/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:67-70/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:67-70/r11.claim: All people return to God's judgment and recompense.
TABRISI:28:67-70/r11.anchor: وإليه } أي وإلى جزائه وحكمه { ترجعون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p441#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p441#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p441#2/r1.claim: The verse affirms God's oneness: He alone is God, and praise belongs to Him in this life and the next.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p441#2/r1.anchor: ثم وحد نفسه فقال: {وهو الله لا إله إلا هو له الحمد في الأولى والآخرة}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p441#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p441#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p441#2/r2.claim: Muqatil says God's allies praise Him in this world and the people of Paradise praise Him in the next.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p441#2/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: يحمده أولياؤه في الدنيا، ويحمدونه في الآخرة يعني: أهل الجنة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p441#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p441#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p441#2/r3.claim: God's judgment means His decision among all creatures.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p441#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p441#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p441#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says this includes God's decree of forgiveness and mercy for the obedient and misery and woe for those who disobey.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p441#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يريد ما حكم لأهل طاعته من المغفرة والرحمة، وما حكم لأهل معصيته من الشقاء والويل

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p606/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p606/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p606/r5.claim: God is praised in the first life and the hereafter, meaning this world and the next.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p606/r5.anchor: له الحمد في الأولى والآخرة { [القصص: 70] في الدنيا والآخرة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p606/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p606/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p606/r7.claim: People return to God on the Day of Resurrection.

ITQAN:v3p37/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p37/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p37/r5.claim: Some paired terms are ordered to match their semantic sequence, as with first and last, before and after, and earlier and later groups; “the first and the last” is an example.
ITQAN:v3p37/r5.anchor: وإما مناسبة لفظ هو من التقدم أو التأخر

ITQAN:v3p235/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p235/r1.speaker: ابن الإصبع
ITQAN:v3p235/r1.claim: Ibn al-Isba‘ defines embedding as concealing one purpose within another; apparent hyperbole in God’s exclusive praise is literally true because He alone owns praise in both worlds.
ITQAN:v3p235/r1.anchor: قال ابن الإصبع هو أن يدمج المتكلم غرضا في غرض أو بديعا في بديع بحيث لا يظهر في الكلام إلا أحد الغرضين

ITQAN:v3p235/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p235/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p235/r2.claim: The author prefers one purpose embedded in another: the verse asserts God’s exclusive praise while alluding to resurrection and recompense.
ITQAN:v3p235/r2.anchor: قلت والأولى أن يقال في هذه الآية إنها من إدماج غرض في غرض فإن الغرض منها تفرده تعالى بوصف الحمد وأدمج فيه الإشارة إلى البعث والجزاء
